main_text.l: XXX.
Postremo recitat Aristoteles gradus deli-
ctorum pugnantium cum iustitia & iure. Alia
inquit, delicta sunt voluntaria, alia inuolun-taria.
XXXI.
In doctrina, quam Iurisconsulti profitentur,
tres gradus delictorum traduntur, dolo facta,
culpa, item casu facta. Et culpae gradus lata, leuis
& leuissima.
XXXII.
Dolus proprie nominatur delictum, ad quod
concurrunt mens sciens quid sit agendum, & vo-
luntas libera contra rectum iudicium faciens.
Hic gradus plurimum habet turpitudinis, quia
maior est contumacia voluntatis, quando mens videt quid agat.
XXXIII.
Culpa lata est, cum quis crassa negligentia
peccat, non tamen affectata, vt cum aliquis re-
bus suis salvis amittit depositum, quia hoc forte
negligentius custodiuit.
XXXIIII.
Etsi autem disputatur, An lata culpa sit do-
lus: tamen recte dicitur, toto genere distare do-

page.notes: The scan shows mirrored show-through text from the other side of the leaf in grey over the whole page; it was left out. No page number, running head or signature is printed. The numerals XXX to XXXIIII stand alone, so they are set as paragraphs. The word "delictorum" is broken at the line end ("deli-" / "ctorum") with no clear printed hyphen, so it is written whole. The first letter of "Etsi" is a decorated capital E. The final "lum" sits apart at the right below the last line, so it is read as the catchword; it completes "do-lum" from the hyphenated word, so the printed text ends on "do-". A stray mark at the bottom centre is not printed text.
